title: Keep the divergence dispatch map a declared, schema-valid registry

facts.note: Task, plan, wagon or acceptance text mentions divergence dispatch or routing of artifacts to trains. Broad terms like 'divergence' only count when they are tied to train dispatch.
Covers planning, implementing, changing, and checking/auditing existing divergence dispatch routing.

values: divergence dispatch routing added, changed, or present as an in-code map instead of registry entries
facts.note: Needs a diff/repo-level observer that detects routing tables defined imperatively in Station Master code instead of read from the declared registry. The source names only the validator test, not a path.
Validator finding from the convention's schema test; needs an observer that consumes validator findings.

fires: A plan or wagon adds an artifact whose divergence must be routed to a train.
A plan or implementation changes which train handles a given artifact_urn on divergence.
Station Master routing is implemented, or already exists, as a hard-coded map or switch in code.
A review or acceptance checks whether the existing divergence dispatch map is a schema-valid registry the Station Master reads.
doesNotFire: Work changes normal train artifact flow without touching divergence dispatch routing.
Work edits documentation or acceptances unrelated to dispatch or train routing.

given: Work plans, implements, changes, or checks how the Station Master routes produced-artifact divergence to trains.
when: The divergence dispatch map is specified, built, modified, or reviewed.
then: The divergence dispatch map itself must be a declared, schema-valid registry (artifact_urn -> train_id) that the Station Master actually reads; routing must never be an imperative in-code map.
prefer: Before planning, locate the repository's existing dispatch registry, its schema and its validator test, and plan changes there. Do not invent a new location or schema.
Plan routing changes as registry entries keyed by artifact_urn mapping to train_id, validated against the registry schema.
Write acceptances that assert the Station Master resolves routes by reading the registry. A plan-only registry paired with an in-code implementation must then fail.
avoid: Routing as a hard-coded map, switch or conditional chain in Station Master code, whether planned or already present.
Registry entries that bypass or fail schema validation.
Treating a registry described only in the plan as compliance when the Station Master does not read it.
why: The source requires divergence routing to be a declared, schema-valid registry that the Station Master reads, not an imperative in-code map.
evidence: Reviewer confirms every divergence route exists as an artifact_urn -> train_id entry in the declared registry, the registry validates against its schema, the Station Master reads it, and no in-code routing map exists.
verifier_detail: Registry shape: map from artifact_urn to train_id; must validate against its schema. Term: dispatch_registry (source term definition is empty).
Detector: flag routing implemented as an imperative in-code map instead of read from the registry; flag a registry the Station Master does not read.
disposition: strict (label as given in the source; the source does not define its enforcement semantics)
